findings.quote: If the two lines are perpendicular, all four angles are $90^\circ$. Check the positions in the figure before writing the equation.
findings.problem: Still open from round 1. The Trap #2 paragraph has four sentences (the set-equal rule, the neighbors sum, the perpendicular case, the check). The limit is one to three short sentences.
findings.source: Checklist L22a; LSG Formatting rules; round-1 read finding 3

findings.quote: The two angles do not have to touch. Each angle in a complementary pair is acute, because the other angle takes up part of the $90^\circ$.
findings.problem: The complementary/supplementary paragraph has four sentences, over the one-to-three limit. The angle paragraph that ends "When only one angle sits at a vertex, we may write just $\angle B$." also has four sentences.
